items.title: Jerry Blumberg Interview, 1961-04-06
items.q: Harold Draub and a friend of mine from Baltimore and myself went into Ryan's to see Bechet... And it was Sidney and Bunk and Harold and my friend and myself.

ctx.x: He'd do things like that repeatedly, yeah. If I remember the other night you mentioned something, some detail escapes me now about Bechet and speaking about when he helped Louis and all that. That's right.

What was that? Well, there was a time when Bechet was playing at Ryan's and Harold Draub and a friend of mine from Baltimore and myself went into Ryan's to see Bechet and Bunk turned up and he had been drinking very heavily. And he was closer in the disorder that they often got in at such times. And he was sitting at our table and then he'd get up to the bandstand and be singing along with the tune. And he was having some kind of contest with Sidney about what... Trying to name tunes that Sidney couldn't…
Actually helped him with his horn.

items.title: Jerry Blumberg Interview, 1961-04-06
items.q: He played Calypso, I mean, that particular piece, like a, like a native Calypso player.

ctx.x: Well, you mentioned the other day about that Calypso that he once went up. What was that?

Yeah, well, there was one time when, when, I guess it was one of those afternoons, I went up there and he said, well, last night I played in a little session, this was up in Harlem, in a bar down the street. And there were a bunch of West Indians there, he said, and I played, we played this tune. And he took out his horn and played some beautiful little Calypso melody that I'd never heard before or since. And I wrote it down. It was so nice, but I, I lost the paper it was written on. But I remember how striking…
By the way, when you did take lessons, did he charge you for it?
